state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You have a misconception about the translation rule for \( f(x - a) \). The correct translation is actually by the vector \( \left[\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ -3 \end{array}\right] \) to shift the graph of \( y=f(x) \) to \( y=f(x-3) \). Remember, the translation is in the opposite direction of the value inside the parentheses.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see! So when it’s \( f(x - a) \), it actually moves the graph down instead of up? That’s kind of confusing because I thought it was just like adding or subtracting normally. Can you explain why it goes in the opposite direction again?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You are correct that the translation for \( f(x - a) \) moves the graph down, not up. This is because the value inside the parentheses affects the x-values, not the y-values. Think of it as shifting the graph horizontally. So, when you see \( f(x - a) \), remember that it shifts the graph to the right by a units.
